column1: # One guard per line: file, test filter, anchor, replacement, separated by TABS.
# A newline inside an anchor is written as a literal backslash-n and expanded by
# the runner. It has to be: a real newline here splits the row, and the reader
# then takes half an anchor and a stray fragment as two malformed entries. That
# happened, and it reported NO-ANCHOR on rows that were fine.
# `scripts/falsify.sh --all` deletes each guard in turn and requires that the
# named test notices. SURVIVED means the guard is described rather than guarded
# -- or, as often, that the mutation and the test are about different things.

column3: guard claimed[port, default: 0] < maximumAddressesPerPort else {\n                addressesRefused += 1
to: query, in: payload, code: DNSCodec.responseCodeRefused, allocator: allocator)\n        else { return }
column4: to: query, in: payload, code: DNSCodec.responseCodeRefused, allocator: allocator)\n        else { return }\n        if true { return }

column3: guard entry.received.count < maximumFragmentsPerDatagram else { return nil }
guard netSwitch.portCount + admitting.pending < limit else { return nil }
column4: guard netSwitch.portCount < limit else { return nil }

column3: flushPerFrame: true, learnsPeer: true, rawDescriptor: descriptor)
